The `test_namespaces.cs` file contains test cases for various C# namespace definitions, including global, traditional, nested, and file-scoped namespaces, demonstrating different class, interface, enum, struct, and record implementations.

# Purpose
This C# source code file demonstrates the use of both traditional and file-scoped namespaces, showcasing the flexibility and organization capabilities of C# namespaces. The file includes a variety of class definitions, interfaces, enums, structs, and records, illustrating how different types of components can be organized within namespaces. The traditional namespace `Com.Example.Traditional` and its nested namespaces demonstrate the hierarchical structure of namespaces, while the file-scoped namespace `Com.Example.FileScoped` highlights the more streamlined syntax introduced in C# 10. The code provides a comprehensive example of how to define and implement classes, interfaces, and other types within these namespaces, offering a clear comparison between the traditional and modern approaches.

The file serves as a practical guide for understanding namespace usage in C#, with a focus on demonstrating the differences and similarities between traditional and file-scoped namespaces. It includes various technical components such as classes with methods, an interface with a method, an enum, a struct, and a record, all within the context of file-scoped namespaces. Additionally, the file illustrates the implementation of an abstract class and its concrete subclass, which also implements an interface, providing a complete example of object-oriented programming principles in C#. This code is intended to be a reference or educational resource rather than an executable program, as it does not contain a `Main` method or entry point.
